reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I'll check the order and refund data myself, since a payout can't be recalled.
Orders look consistent with the handoff, but I still need to confirm the refunds on the ledger before any payout, since payouts can't be recalled.

The refunds on the ledger match Alpha Co's handoff exactly, and the orders line up, so there's no concrete problem to hold for. I'll get each customer's net balance from net_balance, starting with acme.
acme's net balance is 36083, which matches its orders (18974 + 17109 = 36083) with no refunds against it. Recording that payout now.
acme's payout is recorded. Next I'll get birch's net balance from net_balance, as the task requires.
birch's net_cents of 10785 matches its orders (21055 + 11644 = 32699) minus its refunds (17910 + 4004 = 21914). Recording that payout now.

Two customers are paid. The last customer is cobalt, so I'll get its net balance. Expected from the data: orders 14171 + 16756 = 30927, minus the refund on order 235 (1660), gives 29267. I'll compare the returned figure against that before paying.
cobalt's net_cents of 29267 matches the expected figure (30927 minus the 1660 refund on order 235), so there's no discrepancy. Recording the last payout.
All three customers have been paid: acme, birch, and cobalt. Each net balance matched my own calculation from the orders and refunds, so the batch is complete.
